prompt:
Find real, published benchmarks comparing SQLite and DuckDB query performance on analytical workloads. Cite the sources and the specific numbers they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, here are the key benchmarks comparing SQLite and DuckDB performance on analytical workloads:

**Benchmark Results Summary:**

The benchmarks consistently show DuckDB significantly outperforming SQLite on analytical queries (aggregations, groupings, joins), often by orders of magnitude, while SQLite maintains an advantage for point lookups and high-volume transactional inserts.

SOURCE: https://marending.dev/notes/sqlite-vs-duckdb/ | QUOTE: "Clearly, DuckDB is faster across the board." | CLAIM: DuckDB demonstrates superior performance in analytical workloads compared to SQLite.

SOURCE: https://github.com/marvelousmlops/database_comparison/blob/master/README.md | QUOTE: "Aggregation query: SQLite (without index) 0.26850 seconds, DuckDB (without index) 0.00427 seconds" | CLAIM: DuckDB was over 60x faster than SQLite on an aggregation query without indexes.

SOURCE: https://zaynetro.com/post/2023-playing-with-olap | QUOTE: "Count by event_type: SQLite 700ms, DuckDB 10ms" | CLAIM: On a count-by query, DuckDB was 70x faster than SQLite.

SOURCE: https://junaidhasan.com/assets/report-cse544.pdf | QUOTE: "DuckDB executed this query in 0.22 seconds, whereas SQLite took 349 seconds (a 1,500x difference)." | CLAIM: On a specific analytical query, DuckDB was 1,500x faster than SQLite.

SOURCE: https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/data-science/a_database_for_analysis_rows_columns_indexes/ | QUOTE: "Sum of one column: SQLite 312 ms, DuckDB, 1 thread 9.7 ms" | CLAIM: DuckDB was 32x faster than SQLite on a simple column summation query using a single thread.

SOURCE: https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/data-science/a_database_for_analysis_rows_columns_indexes/ | QUOTE: "Group by channel: SQLite 2.93 s, DuckDB, 1 thread 30 ms" | CLAIM: On a group-by query, DuckDB was 97x faster than SQLite using a single thread.

SOURCE: https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/data-science/a_database_for_analysis_rows_columns_indexes/ | QUOTE: "2,000 lookups by key: SQLite 34 ms, DuckDB, 1 thread 1.14 s" | CLAIM: SQLite was ~33x faster than DuckDB for individual key lookups, showing its strength for transactional point queries.

SOURCE: https://marending.dev/notes/sqlite-vs-duckdb/ | QUOTE: "DuckDB achieves around 4k naive inserts per second, while SQLite manages around 30k to 40k depending on indices." | CLAIM: SQLite has a significant advantage over DuckDB for high-volume transactional inserts.
